Accessories swapped, including ECG/RESP cable, ECG trunk cable, lead set, electrodes, or patient cable.
Power behavior, including whether the alarm cleared after a safe restart or returned immediately after power cycle.
Environmental factors, including motion, artifact, poor electrode contact, fluid contamination, or cable strain.
Indicator lights, module recognition behavior, MMS connection status, or other parameter INOP messages observed.
Final device status, including whether the monitor, MMS, parameter module, or accessory was returned to service or labeled Out of Service.

title: Philips IntelliVue MX Series Patient Monitor - Will Not Power On or Randomly Shuts Down
description: Troubleshooting startup failure or unexpected shutdown caused by AC power, power cords, batteries, docking connections, accessories, overheating, or intermittent external connections.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an IntelliVue monitor while it is the only device supporting an actively monitored patient. Notify the clinical team that monitoring may be interrupted. Transfer the patient to another verified monitor when continuous monitoring is required. Confirm that all required physiological parameters and alarms are available on the replacement device. Do not assume an unexpected shutdown is only an equipment problem. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues without relying on the affected monitor. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the monitor can be safely removed from patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the monitor: Does not respond when the power button is pressed; Starts only when connected to AC power; Starts on battery but shuts down shortly afterward; Shuts down when moved or disconnected from AC power; Restarts repeatedly; Loses power when the cart, mount, or power cord is disturbed; Displays a low-battery, battery malfunction, power interruption, or temperature-related message; Produces any unusual sound, heat, or odor. Record the AC power indicator, battery indicator, startup behavior, displayed messages, and approximate runtime before shutdown. Expected outcome: The failure pattern is clearly identified before components are exchanged.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Immediate Safety Concerns
steps.instructions: Disconnect the monitor from AC power and inspect for: Damaged or crushed power cords; Bent, loose, or discolored connectors; Liquid intrusion; Cracked housings; Loose battery doors or covers; Battery swelling or leakage; Burn marks; Unusual heat or electrical odor. Do not continue powering the monitor when liquid damage, battery swelling, overheating, smoke, or an electrical odor is present. Expected outcome: No visible condition requiring immediate removal from service is found. If damage, excessive heat, or odor is present, stop troubleshooting and send the device for repair evaluation.

steps.title: 4. Verify the AC Outlet
steps.instructions: Test the wall outlet using an approved outlet tester or another known-good device. When the monitor is connected through a power strip, isolation transformer, ceiling service column, UPS, or cart outlet, test the original wall outlet directly when permitted. Expected outcome: The outlet provides stable and correctly wired facility power. If the outlet fails testing, use a verified outlet and report the facility power issue through the appropriate department.

steps.title: 5. Check the Power Cord and External Power Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect and reseat the power cord at: The wall outlet; The monitor or external power supply; Any cart, docking station, or mounting power connection. Confirm that each connection is fully seated and does not move excessively. Replace the power cord with a compatible, known-good hospital-grade cord when available. Expected outcome: The AC indicator remains stable and the monitor powers on normally. If replacing or reseating the cord resolves the issue, complete an operational test and stop.

steps.title: 6. Inspect the External Power Supply, If Equipped
steps.instructions: Some MX configurations use an external power supply or receive power through an attached docking or mounting system. Check for: A disconnected AC input; A loose low-voltage output connector; A damaged power-supply cable; Missing or abnormal power-supply indicators; Excessive heat; Power interruption when the cable is gently moved. Test with a known-good compatible power supply only when approved by the facility and manufacturer configuration. Expected outcome: Stable power reaches the monitor without interruption. If a known-good external supply corrects the problem, replace the defective supply and verify normal operation.

steps.title: 7. Attempt a Controlled Power-On Using AC Power
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external accessories and connect the monitor directly to verified AC power. Press the power button normally. Do not repeatedly cycle power in rapid succession. Observe: AC power indicator; Display illumination; Fan or startup sounds, when applicable; Philips startup screen; Error messages; Whether the monitor completes startup or shuts down during boot. Expected outcome: The monitor completes startup and remains powered. If the monitor remains completely unresponsive despite verified AC input, proceed toward bench evaluation.

steps.title: 8. Check the Battery Installation and Condition
steps.instructions: For models equipped with removable batteries: Power the monitor off. Disconnect AC power. Inspect the battery compartment and battery contacts externally. Confirm that each approved battery is fully seated and latched. Check for swelling, cracks, contamination, corrosion, or damaged contacts. Verify that the battery is the correct type for the monitor. Do not use swollen, leaking, physically damaged, or excessively hot batteries. Expected outcome: Approved batteries are installed securely with no visible damage. If reseating the battery restores operation, reconnect AC power, confirm charging, and complete a battery transfer test.

steps.title: 9. Test AC-Only Operation
steps.instructions: When the model and facility procedure permit, remove questionable removable batteries and operate the monitor from verified AC power. Observe the monitor for the duration necessary to reproduce the reported shutdown. Expected outcome: The monitor remains powered continuously on AC. If the monitor operates normally without the battery, the battery may be defective or causing unstable power behavior. Replace it with an approved, known-good battery and retest.

steps.title: 10. Test With a Known-Good Battery
steps.instructions: Install a charged, compatible, known-good battery. Confirm that: The battery is recognized; The battery indicator appears; Charging begins when AC power is connected; The monitor remains on when AC power is removed; The battery percentage does not drop unexpectedly. Expected outcome: The monitor operates normally during transition between AC and battery power. If the known-good battery resolves the issue, remove the failed battery from service and process it according to facility battery-handling procedures.

steps.title: 11. Check for Power Loss During Movement
steps.instructions: With the monitor off the patient and operating under controlled conditions, gently check whether power is interrupted when: The AC cord is moved; The external power connector is moved; The monitor is placed into or removed from its dock; The cart or mounting arm is repositioned; The battery compartment is lightly pressed. Do not force or sharply bend connectors. Expected outcome: Power remains stable during normal handling. If movement causes shutdown, suspect a worn connector, damaged cable, loose docking interface, battery-contact problem, or internal power connection. Remove the monitor from service.

steps.title: 12. Disconnect Nonessential Accessories
steps.instructions: Power the monitor off and disconnect nonessential external equipment, including: USB devices; Barcode scanners; Printers; External displays; Network adapters; Unnecessary measurement modules; Third-party accessories; Auxiliary communication devices. Restart the monitor using only the minimum required configuration. Expected outcome: The monitor starts and remains powered without the external accessories. If normal operation returns, reconnect accessories individually until the device causing the shutdown is identified. Remove the failed accessory from service.

steps.title: 13. Check for Overheating or Blocked Ventilation
steps.instructions: Inspect the monitor’s external ventilation openings. Confirm that they are not blocked by: Bedding; Dust accumulation; Labels; Mounting hardware; Equipment stacked against the monitor; Improper placement inside an enclosure. Allow an overheated monitor to cool while disconnected from the patient and AC power. Do not insert tools or compressed air into the monitor unless specifically permitted by an approved maintenance procedure. Expected outcome: Ventilation is unobstructed and the monitor operates without excessive heat. If shutdown occurs only after warming up, remove the monitor from service for fan, thermal-sensor, power-supply, or internal component evaluation.

steps.title: 14. Review Available Logs or Shutdown Messages
steps.instructions: When accessible through approved Clinical Engineering procedures, review the monitor’s status information or error logs for: Low-battery shutdown; Battery communication failure; Unexpected restart; Power interruption; Excessive temperature; Software startup failure; Hardware malfunction. Record error codes and timestamps without changing configuration settings unnecessarily. Expected outcome: Available information helps distinguish external power loss from an internal hardware or software failure. Do not clear logs before documenting relevant findings.

steps.title: 15. Perform a Controlled Operational Test
steps.instructions: After correcting an external issue: Start the monitor on AC power. Confirm that startup completes normally. Verify the AC and battery indicators. Allow the battery to charge. Disconnect AC power and verify uninterrupted battery operation. Reconnect AC power and confirm uninterrupted transfer. Operate the monitor long enough to evaluate the reported shutdown condition. Verify the display, controls, alarms, parameters, and network connection as applicable. Complete electrical safety testing when required by facility policy or following repair. Expected outcome: The monitor remains powered during startup, stationary operation, movement, and AC-to-battery transitions. If the device shuts down again, stop troubleshooting and escalate the repair.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Philips IntelliVue MX monitor shut down without warning when disconnected from AC power.
CCR.Cause: Testing found that the installed battery was recognized but could not support the monitor during the AC-to-battery transfer; the monitor operated normally with a known-good battery.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the failed battery, verified charging, completed AC-to-battery transfer and operational testing, and returned the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: Monitor tested directly from wall power
External power supply or docking connection tested
Shutdown occurred on AC, battery, or both
Error messages or log entries recorded
Unusual heat, odor, or visible damage documented
Electrical safety test completed when required

title: Philips IntelliVue MX Series Patient Monitor - Battery Not Charging or Short Runtime
description: Troubleshooting batteries that will not charge, discharge rapidly, show incorrect status, or fail to support the monitor during transport or power loss.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot battery performance while the IntelliVue monitor is the only device supporting an actively monitored patient. If continuous monitoring is required: Notify the clinical team that battery operation may be unreliable. Connect the monitor to verified AC power. Transfer the patient to another verified monitor before disconnecting power or testing battery runtime. Do not transport a patient using a monitor with questionable battery capacity. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues without relying on an unreliable battery. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the monitor can be safely removed from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported issue is: Battery not detected; Battery not charging; Charge percentage not increasing; Battery discharging while connected to AC power; Unexpected shutdown when AC power is removed; Runtime significantly shorter than expected; Battery or charger malfunction message; Blinking or abnormal battery indicator. Document the displayed battery percentage, charging symbol, indicator behavior, and any technical messages. Expected outcome: The specific battery symptom is identified before components are replaced.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Monitor Is Receiving AC Power
steps.instructions: Confirm that: The power cord is fully inserted into the monitor or external power supply. The cord is connected to an approved hospital-grade outlet. The monitor displays its AC power indication. The power cord and plug have no cuts, bent contacts, discoloration, or heat damage. Test the outlet with an approved electrical tester or connect the monitor to another known-good outlet. Expected outcome: The monitor recognizes AC power and begins charging. If charging begins after changing outlets, correct the outlet or power-source issue and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Test With a Known-Good Power Cord
steps.instructions: Substitute a compatible, known-good hospital-grade power cord when applicable. Inspect removable power-supply connections, docking connections, or external adapters used by the specific MX configuration. Expected outcome: Stable AC power is restored and the charging indicator appears. If charging resumes, remove the defective cord or power accessory from service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Check the Battery Installation
steps.instructions: Power down the monitor when clinically safe and inspect the battery compartment externally. Confirm that: The battery is the correct type for the specific MX model. The battery is fully inserted and latched. No foreign material obstructs the compartment. Accessible battery contacts are clean, dry, and undamaged. The battery casing is not cracked, swollen, leaking, or deformed. Do not use a damaged or swollen battery. Expected outcome: The battery is securely installed and recognized by the monitor. If reseating the battery restores detection or charging, verify operation and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Review Battery and Charging Indicators
steps.instructions: Reconnect the monitor to AC power and observe the battery symbol, charge percentage, LEDs, and technical messages. Depending on the MX model, a charging indication may appear yellow, while a blinking red battery indicator may identify a battery or charging malfunction. Allow several minutes for the displayed charging status to update. Expected outcome: The monitor indicates that the battery is installed and charging without malfunction messages.

steps.title: 7. Allow the Battery to Reach Normal Temperature
steps.instructions: A battery that is unusually hot or cold may not charge normally. Move the monitor and battery to a controlled indoor environment and allow them to reach room temperature. Do not apply external heat or place the battery near a cooling source. Check for: Unusual heat; Chemical odor; Swelling; Leakage; Discoloration. Expected outcome: Charging begins after the battery returns to a normal operating temperature. Remove any battery showing physical damage, odor, leakage, or excessive heat from service immediately.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Known-Good Compatible Battery
steps.instructions: Install a charged, known-good battery approved for the specific IntelliVue MX model. Observe whether: The replacement battery is detected. The charging symbol appears. The charge percentage increases. The monitor remains operating when AC power is briefly disconnected. Expected outcome: The known-good battery charges and supports the monitor normally. If the known-good battery operates correctly, replace the original battery and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 9. Evaluate Short Runtime
steps.instructions: Fully charge the battery while the monitor is connected to verified AC power. Confirm that the displayed charge reaches the expected full-charge condition. Disconnect AC power and operate the monitor under a controlled test configuration. Record: Starting charge percentage; Start time; Connected modules and accessories; Display brightness; Alarm activity; Shutdown time or remaining charge. Compare the observed runtime with the facility’s acceptance criteria and the applicable Philips service documentation for that exact MX model and battery type. Expected outcome: The battery provides acceptable runtime without sudden percentage drops or unexpected shutdown. A battery that charges but provides inadequate runtime should be replaced.

steps.title: 10. Check for Excessive External Power Demand
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external accessories during bench testing, such as: USB devices; Barcode scanners; External recorders; Unnecessary measurement modules; Powered interface accessories. Return display brightness and configuration settings to normal operating levels. Expected outcome: Battery discharge becomes stable after a defective or high-demand accessory is removed. If one accessory causes abnormal discharge, remove that accessory from service and evaluate it separately.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Controlled Power-Transfer Test
steps.instructions: With a known-good battery installed and the monitor operating on AC power: Confirm that the battery is detected and adequately charged. Disconnect AC power. Verify that the monitor transfers to battery operation without restarting. Reconnect AC power. Verify that AC operation and charging resume. Do not perform this test while the monitor is connected to a patient. Expected outcome: The monitor transfers between AC and battery power without interruption, restart, or battery malfunction.

steps.title: 12. Complete Required Performance and Safety Checks
steps.instructions: After replacing a battery or resolving an external power issue: Verify AC operation. Verify charging indication. Verify battery operation. Confirm stable AC-to-battery transfer. Check for technical alarms. Perform electrical safety testing when required by facility policy. Confirm the monitor is safe for clinical use. Expected outcome: The monitor passes operational and safety verification before being returned to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Philips IntelliVue MX monitor showed a full battery but shut down shortly after AC power was disconnected.
CCR.Cause: The installed battery was detected and charged normally but failed the controlled runtime test; a known-good battery operated the monitor without interruption.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the degraded battery, verified charging and AC-to-battery transfer, completed an acceptable runtime test, and returned the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: Battery age or installation date recorded
Unusual heat, swelling, odor, or leakage

title: Philips IntelliVue MX Series Patient Monitor - Measurement Module or Module Rack Not Recognized
description: Troubleshooting missing measurement modules or racks caused by seating, connection, power, compatibility, configuration, communication, or accessory failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unrecognized measurement module or module rack while the IntelliVue monitor is the only device supporting an active patient. Notify the clinical team that the affected parameters may be unavailable. Verify the patient using another approved clinical method. Transfer monitoring to another verified monitor when continuous monitoring is required. Do not assume missing measurements are only an equipment problem. Expected outcome: Required patient monitoring continues without relying on the unrecognized module or rack. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the equipment can be safely removed from active patient use.

steps.title: Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Observe the monitor and document which measurement module is not recognized, whether the entire rack is missing or only one module, whether the module appears intermittently, any displayed equipment malfunction, incompatible device, or communication message, and whether the issue began after transport, cleaning, module replacement, software work, or relocation. Check whether other measurements from the monitor remain available. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to a specific module, rack position, rack assembly, or monitor connection.

steps.title: Inspect the Module and Rack Externally
steps.instructions: Remove the device from clinical use and inspect for a module that is not fully inserted, bent, recessed, contaminated, or damaged contacts, cracked module housings, damaged rack slots or guide rails, debris or dried cleaning residue, signs of liquid intrusion, and unusual heat, odor, or discoloration. Do not insert tools into electrical contacts or use unapproved cleaning fluids. Expected outcome: No visible obstruction, contamination, or physical damage prevents proper connection. If liquid intrusion, overheating, or damaged contacts are found, stop troubleshooting and remove the affected equipment from service.

steps.title: Reseat the Measurement Module
steps.instructions: With the monitor and rack in a safe condition, remove the affected module, inspect its connector and housing, reinsert it fully into the rack until it is properly seated, and allow the monitor sufficient time to detect and initialize it. Observe whether the parameter label, waveform area, or module indicator appears. Expected outcome: The module is recognized and its available measurements appear. If reseating resolves the issue, perform a functional verification and stop.

steps.title: Test a Different Rack Position
steps.instructions: When the rack design permits, move the affected module to another compatible slot. If the module works in another slot, suspect the original rack position or its connection. If the module remains unrecognized in multiple slots, suspect the module, compatibility, or system configuration. If several modules fail only in one section of the rack, suspect the rack rather than each individual module. Expected outcome: Testing distinguishes a module-specific problem from a rack-slot problem. Do not force a module into a slot that is not mechanically or functionally compatible.

steps.title: Test With a Known-Good Compatible Module
steps.instructions: Install a verified, compatible measurement module of the same type when available. Confirm that the replacement module is approved for the monitor model and installed software revision. Do not use compatibility based only on physical fit. Allow the monitor to complete module initialization. Expected outcome: A known-good module working normally indicates that the original module is defective or incompatible. A known-good module also failing suggests a rack, connection, configuration, or monitor-side issue. If the known-good module is recognized, remove the original module from service and stop.

steps.title: Check the Module Rack Connection
steps.instructions: Inspect all accessible external connections between the module rack and the IntelliVue monitor. Verify that the rack cable is fully seated at both ends, connector locking mechanisms are engaged, the cable is not pinched, stretched, sharply bent, or damaged, no adapter, extension, or docking connection is loose, the cable is connected to the correct designated interface, and the rack is securely attached to its mounting or docking arrangement. Disconnect and reconnect external rack cables only after patient use has ended and according to facility procedure. Expected outcome: The rack establishes a stable communication and power connection with the monitor. If reconnecting the cable restores recognition, inspect the cable and connectors carefully before returning the system to service.

steps.title: Verify Rack Power and Status Indicators
steps.instructions: Check whether the rack has applicable power or status indicators. Document whether indicators are illuminated normally, completely off, flashing unexpectedly, changing when the rack cable is moved, or different from an identical functioning system. If the entire rack is unrecognized and all indicators are off, verify its external power source or monitor connection, depending on the installed configuration. Expected outcome: The rack shows stable indications consistent with normal power and communication. Intermittent indicators or recognition when a cable is moved suggests a damaged connector, cable, or rack interface.

steps.title: Substitute the Rack Cable
steps.instructions: When a separate replaceable communication cable is used, test with a known-good compatible cable. Do not substitute visually similar cables unless their compatibility has been verified. Expected outcome: Recognition with the replacement cable identifies the original cable as defective. Continued failure directs troubleshooting toward the rack or monitor interface. If the replacement cable resolves the issue, label the defective cable and remove it from service.

steps.title: Test the Rack on a Known-Good Compatible Monitor
steps.instructions: When available and permitted by facility procedure, connect the rack to another compatible IntelliVue monitor. Use only a monitor with compatible hardware and software. Do not transfer patient data or configurations unintentionally. Perform the test without an active patient. Expected outcome: If the rack works on another monitor, suspect the original monitor’s interface or configuration. If the rack fails on both monitors, suspect the rack, cable, or attached module.

steps.title: Test a Known-Good Rack on the Original Monitor
steps.instructions: Connect a verified compatible rack and cable to the original monitor. Expected outcome: If the known-good rack is recognized, the original rack or cable is defective. If the known-good rack is also not recognized, suspect the monitor connection, configuration, or internal communication path. If the monitor fails to recognize multiple known-good racks, discontinue field troubleshooting.

steps.title: Review Module Compatibility
steps.instructions: Confirm that the module and rack are supported by the specific IntelliVue MX model, the installed monitor software revision, the rack type and interface, the facility’s licensed options and configuration, and any required Philips system components. A module may physically fit but remain unavailable because of hardware, software, licensing, or configuration incompatibility. Expected outcome: The installed module and rack are confirmed as supported components. If compatibility cannot be verified, do not condemn the module. Escalate using its complete model, part number, and software information.

steps.title: Check Monitor Configuration and Measurement Availability
steps.instructions: Review accessible configuration information and confirm that the expected measurement is enabled, the parameter has not been intentionally disabled, the selected screen configuration is not hiding the measurement, the monitor is not operating under an incompatible profile, and no duplicate or conflicting measurement source is preventing normal display. Do not alter protected configuration settings without authorization and a documented backup or approved configuration process. Expected outcome: The measurement is enabled and available for display when the hardware is detected. If a setting correction resolves the problem, verify the approved configuration before returning the monitor to service.

steps.title: Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: After all modules and cables are securely connected, shut down the monitor using the normal shutdown process, disconnect external AC power when appropriate, allow the system to power down completely, restore power and restart the monitor, and observe module and rack initialization during startup. Do not repeatedly cycle power or interrupt a software update. Expected outcome: The monitor completes startup and recognizes the connected rack and modules. If recognition returns only temporarily, treat the issue as intermittent and continue escalation.

steps.title: Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After the module or rack is recognized, confirm the module remains detected without interruption, verify each affected parameter using an approved simulator or test device, confirm expected waveforms and numerical values, check for equipment malfunction messages, gently inspect cable stability without stressing connectors, verify alarm generation for the affected parameters when required, and confirm the approved monitor configuration remains intact. Expected outcome: The rack and modules remain recognized and all affected measurements pass functional testing. Do not return the monitor to service based only on the module icon reappearing.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the IntelliVue MX monitor did not recognize the measurement module rack and the connected parameters were unavailable.
CCR.Cause: Testing with known-good modules and cables confirmed that the original rack failed in multiple compatible monitor connections.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the defective module rack from service, installed a verified replacement rack, and confirmed all connected measurements using approved patient simulators.

helpfulDetails: Signs of liquid intrusion or physical damage

title: Philips IntelliVue MX Series Patient Monitor - ECG Lead-Off, Artifact, or No Waveform
description: Troubleshooting missing or unstable ECG waveforms caused by electrodes, lead wires, patient cables, connections, placement, settings, or acquisition hardware.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the IntelliVue monitor is the only device providing required cardiac monitoring to an active patient. Notify the clinical team that the ECG signal is unavailable or unreliable. Assess the patient using another approved clinical method. Move the patient to another verified monitor when continuous ECG monitoring is required. Do not assume an abnormal or missing waveform is only an equipment problem. Expected outcome: Required cardiac monitoring continues without relying on the affected ECG channel. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the equipment can be safely evaluated.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Observe and document whether the monitor displays: ECG Leads Off; a specific electrode or lead-off indication; a flat or missing waveform; excessive artifact or baseline movement; dashed heart-rate values; an ECG waveform without a calculated heart rate; intermittent signal loss when the cable is moved. Confirm whether the problem affects all ECG leads or only a selected lead. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified before components are replaced.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Electrode Placement and Skin Contact
steps.instructions: Verify that: All required electrodes are attached. Electrodes are positioned correctly for the selected lead configuration. Electrode gel is not dried out. Electrodes are not expired, damaged, or contaminated. The skin is clean, dry, and properly prepared. Excessive hair is not preventing electrode contact. Poor electrode-to-skin contact is a common cause of lead-off messages and ECG artifact. Philips documentation emphasizes proper skin preparation and electrode contact for obtaining a clear ECG signal. Replace questionable electrodes with a new approved set. Expected outcome: The lead-off indication clears and a stable waveform appears. If resolved, verify operation and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Check Electrode Snaps and Lead-Wire Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect each lead wire where it connects to the electrode. Confirm every snap, clip, or connector is fully attached. Look for loose snaps, bent contacts, corrosion, dried gel, or contamination. Ensure lead wires are not pulling against the electrodes. Disconnect and reconnect each lead individually. Expected outcome: Each electrode maintains a secure electrical connection without intermittent lead-off indications.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the ECG Patient Cable
steps.instructions: Examine the full patient cable and lead-wire set for: Cuts, cracks, stretching, or crushed sections; exposed conductors; bent or recessed connector pins; fluid intrusion or residue; loose strain reliefs; damage near the trunk connector or lead-wire junctions. Gently flex accessible cable sections while observing the waveform. Do not aggressively manipulate a cable connected to a patient. Expected outcome: The ECG signal remains stable when the cable is handled normally. If the waveform drops out or artifact appears consistently during cable movement, replace the affected cable or lead-wire set.

steps.title: 6. Reseat the ECG Cable at the Acquisition Device
steps.instructions: Disconnect and firmly reconnect the ECG patient cable at the IntelliVue measurement module, Multi-Measurement Module, X-series module, or other connected acquisition device. Check that: The connector is fully seated. The connector orientation is correct. No pins are bent or damaged. The socket is clean and dry. The module itself is fully connected to the monitor. Expected outcome: The monitor recognizes the ECG connection and displays a stable waveform.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Using approved and compatible components, substitute one item at a time: Electrodes; lead-wire set; ECG trunk cable; compatible measurement module or acquisition device, when available. Do not replace multiple components simultaneously unless patient safety requires immediate equipment exchange. Expected outcome: The defective accessory is isolated without incorrectly condemning the monitor. If a known-good accessory resolves the issue, remove the failed accessory from service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Verify the Selected ECG Lead and Cable Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that the monitor configuration matches the connected cable, such as: 3-lead; 5-lead; 6-lead; 10-lead or 12-lead acquisition configuration, when applicable. Verify that: An available ECG lead is selected for display. The selected primary and secondary leads are appropriate. The displayed waveform has not been turned off. ECG is not being sourced from an unintended monitoring device. The waveform size or gain is not set so low that the signal appears absent. The IntelliVue platform provides configurable ECG lead, waveform, gain, and display settings that can affect how the ECG appears. Expected outcome: The monitor displays an available ECG lead at a usable waveform size.

steps.title: 9. Eliminate Common Sources of Artifact
steps.instructions: Check for external conditions that can distort the ECG signal: Patient movement, shivering, tremors, or muscle tension; loose or poorly adhered electrodes; lead wires pulling on electrodes; ECG cables routed alongside power cords; powered beds, warming devices, pumps, or other electrical equipment; damaged grounding or power accessories; excess moisture on the patient or cables. Temporarily separate the ECG cable from nearby power cords and nonessential equipment when safe. Expected outcome: The waveform becomes stable after the external interference or mechanical cause is removed.

steps.title: 10. Compare AC Power and Battery Operation
steps.instructions: When supported by the specific MX model, observe ECG operation: While connected to approved AC power; while operating briefly on a sufficiently charged battery. Use only normal operating controls. Do not defeat grounding or electrical safety protections. If artifact occurs only on AC power, investigate the outlet, power supply, grounding path, and nearby equipment according to facility procedures. Expected outcome: ECG performance remains stable under both normal power conditions.

steps.title: 11. Restart the Monitor When Clinically Safe
steps.instructions: After confirming that the patient is supported by another monitor: Perform a normal shutdown. Disconnect unnecessary accessories. Restart the monitor according to standard operating procedures. Reconnect the ECG acquisition equipment and known-good patient cable. Observe the startup process for module or measurement errors. Expected outcome: The ECG measurement initializes normally and produces a stable waveform. If the issue resolves after restart, complete functional verification before returning the monitor to service.

steps.title: 12. Test the ECG Channel With an Approved Simulator
steps.instructions: Connect an approved patient simulator using known-good ECG accessories. Verify: A waveform is displayed. The simulated heart rate is measured correctly. Multiple selectable leads produce reasonable waveforms. No lead-off message remains. The waveform stays stable while the cable remains stationary. Alarm operation is verified according to facility procedure. Do not use a patient as the functional test source. Expected outcome: The monitor accurately displays and calculates the simulated ECG signal. If the monitor passes with the simulator, the original cause was likely related to electrodes, patient preparation, accessory condition, placement, or the clinical environment.

steps.title: 13. Isolate the Acquisition Device
steps.instructions: When another compatible, verified acquisition device is available: Test the original acquisition device on a known-good monitor. Test a known-good acquisition device on the affected monitor. Maintain compatibility with the specific IntelliVue model and software configuration. Expected outcome: The failure follows either the acquisition device or the monitor, identifying the appropriate component for repair evaluation. Do not interchange modules unless compatibility and configuration are confirmed.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported an ECG Leads Off message with intermittent artifact and no reliable ECG waveform on the Philips IntelliVue MX monitor.
CCR.Cause: Testing found an intermittent open connection in the ECG lead-wire set near the patient connector; the monitor passed simulator testing with known-good accessories.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the damaged lead-wire set, verified stable ECG waveforms and heart-rate readings with a patient simulator, confirmed alarm operation, and returned the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: Patient was transferred to another monitoring device
Exact lead-off or ECG message recorded
Skin preparation and electrode placement checked
Known-good cables or lead wires tested
ECG settings and selected lead verified

title: Philips IntelliVue MX Series Patient Monitor - SpO2 Sensor Not Detected or No Saturation Reading
description: Troubleshooting absent or intermittent SpO2 readings caused by sensor, adapter cable, connection, placement, perfusion, configuration, or measurement-hardware issues.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the IntelliVue monitor is the only device assessing an active patient’s oxygenation. If continuous SpO2 monitoring is clinically required: Notify the clinical team that the SpO2 measurement is unavailable or unreliable. Assess the patient using another approved clinical method. Transfer SpO2 monitoring to another verified monitor or pulse oximeter. Treat unexpectedly low or missing values as a potential clinical condition until confirmed otherwise. Expected outcome: Patient assessment continues without relying on the affected SpO2 channel. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the monitor can be safely removed from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Observe the SpO2 parameter area and document whether the monitor shows: No sensor detected; Sensor disconnected; No pulse; Searching or question marks; Dashed SpO2 and pulse values; Intermittent readings; An SpO2 equipment malfunction or technical alarm; A waveform without a numeric value; No SpO2 parameter area at all. Also determine whether the problem began after cleaning, transport, accessory replacement, software configuration, or connection of a measurement module. Expected outcome: The symptom and displayed technical message are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Confirm the SpO2 Measurement Is Available and Enabled
steps.instructions: Verify that the monitor configuration includes an SpO2 measurement source and that the SpO2 parameter is switched on. Depending on the IntelliVue MX model and configuration, SpO2 may be provided through: A built-in measurement connector; An X2 or X3 measurement device; A Multi-Measurement Module; A compatible measurement extension; A configured Philips FAST, Masimo, or Nellcor SpO2 interface. Do not assume sensors from different SpO2 technologies are interchangeable. Expected outcome: The appropriate SpO2 measurement source is present, recognized, and enabled. Philips documentation indicates that IntelliVue monitors automatically activate SpO2 when a compatible sensor is connected, subject to system configuration. If the SpO2 parameter remains absent despite a recognized measurement source, proceed to configuration review or escalation.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Sensor and Adapter Cable
steps.instructions: Disconnect the sensor and inspect the complete accessory path for: Bent, recessed, corroded, or contaminated contacts; Cracked connector housings; Cut, pinched, stretched, or frayed cable insulation; Fluid intrusion or cleaning residue; Damaged sensor emitters or detector surfaces; Loose connections between the sensor and adapter cable; Incorrect sensor type or incompatible connector. Do not use an accessory that is visibly damaged, contaminated internally, or excessively warm. Expected outcome: The sensor and adapter cable are clean, dry, physically intact, and compatible with the installed SpO2 technology. If damage is found, replace the affected accessory and stop if normal operation returns.

steps.title: 5. Reseat Every SpO2 Connection
steps.instructions: Disconnect and firmly reconnect: The patient sensor from the adapter cable, when applicable. The adapter cable from the monitor or measurement module. The X2, X3, Multi-Measurement Module, or measurement extension from the host monitor, when applicable. Confirm that each connection seats completely and cannot be removed with light movement. Expected outcome: The monitor recognizes the sensor and begins displaying a plethysmographic waveform, pulse rate, and saturation value. If the measurement returns, perform a functional check and stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify Sensor Placement and Test Conditions
steps.instructions: When testing with an approved simulator or a clinically appropriate test subject, verify that: The sensor is positioned according to its intended orientation. The light emitter and detector are aligned across the tissue. The application site is clean and dry. The sensor is secure but not excessively tight. Strong ambient light is blocked when it may affect the sensor. There is no significant motion during the test. Nail coverings, artificial nails, or other obstructions are not interfering with the optical path. Do not use a staff member as the sole quantitative accuracy standard. Use an approved SpO2 simulator when verification of displayed values is required. Expected outcome: A stable pleth waveform and saturation value appear under controlled conditions.

steps.title: 7. Evaluate Signal Quality and Perfusion
steps.instructions: If the sensor is detected but no reliable value appears, observe: Plethysmographic waveform quality; Signal-quality or perfusion indicators; Pulse rate agreement with another verified source; Motion or repeated artifact; Intermittent waveform loss. Low perfusion, motion, venous pulsation, incorrect placement, or excessive ambient light may prevent a stable reading even when the monitor and sensor are functioning. Expected outcome: A stable waveform and pulse value are obtained under controlled test conditions. If the device works with a simulator but not in the reported clinical situation, document that the monitor passed testing and advise the clinical department to evaluate sensor selection, placement, motion, and perfusion conditions.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Sensor
steps.instructions: Connect a known-good, approved sensor that matches the monitor’s installed SpO2 technology. Do not cross-connect Philips FAST, Masimo, or Nellcor accessories unless the specific cable and measurement hardware are designed for that technology. Expected outcome: The monitor detects the replacement sensor and displays a stable reading. If the replacement works, remove the original sensor from use. If the failure remains, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 9. Substitute the Adapter or Interface Cable
steps.instructions: When the sensor connects through a separate adapter or patient cable, replace that cable with a known-good compatible cable. Flex the original cable gently near both connector ends while observing the measurement. Do not continue using a cable that causes the reading to appear or disappear with movement. Expected outcome: Stable operation with the replacement cable identifies the original cable as defective. If resolved, replace the failed cable and stop.

steps.title: 10. Test Another SpO2 Input or Measurement Source
steps.instructions: When available, connect the known-good sensor and cable to another compatible: IntelliVue monitor; X2 or X3; Multi-Measurement Module; SpO2 measurement extension. Then test a known-good measurement source on the affected host monitor. This controlled swap helps isolate the failure to: The sensor; The adapter cable; The measurement module; The host monitor; The system configuration. Expected outcome: The failure follows one specific accessory or measurement source. Remove the failed component from service when identified.

steps.title: 11. Check the Measurement Module Connection
steps.instructions: If SpO2 is supplied through an X2, X3, Multi-Measurement Module, or measurement extension: Confirm the module is fully seated. Verify that the host monitor recognizes the module. Check whether other measurements from the same module are available. Inspect accessible connector surfaces for damage or contamination. Test the module on another compatible host, when authorized. Test a known-good module on the affected monitor. The IntelliVue platform can obtain measurements through scalable measurement modules and companion devices, depending on the specific MX configuration. Expected outcome: The SpO2 failure is isolated to either the removable measurement source or the host monitor.

steps.title: 12. Review SpO2 Settings and Source Selection
steps.instructions: Verify that: SpO2 is switched on. The expected SpO2 source is selected. The parameter has not been removed from the active screen. An alternate SpO2 source is not taking priority. The selected patient category is appropriate. The current profile has not disabled or hidden the measurement. Automatic measurement behavior has not switched SpO2 off after sensor removal. Philips configuration documentation warns that certain automatic on/off configurations may unintentionally switch SpO2 off after the sensor is removed under specific alarm conditions. Do not change institutional profiles or protected settings without authorization. Record the original setting before making any approved change. Expected outcome: The correct SpO2 source is enabled and visible.

steps.title: 13. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: After removing the monitor from patient use: Disconnect unnecessary accessories. Shut down the monitor using the normal power procedure. Disconnect external power if permitted. Allow the system to fully power down. Reconnect the measurement module and known-good SpO2 accessories. Restart the monitor and observe startup messages. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a monitor displaying persistent hardware, safety, or service errors. Expected outcome: The monitor completes startup, recognizes the measurement hardware, and detects the sensor. If the problem clears, complete a functional verification before returning the device to service.

steps.title: 14. Verify Operation with Approved Test Equipment
steps.instructions: Use a compatible SpO2 simulator and approved accessories to verify: Sensor or simulator detection; Pleth waveform presentation; SpO2 numeric display; Pulse-rate display; Technical alarm behavior when the sensor is disconnected; Measurement recovery after reconnection; Stability when the cable is gently moved; Agreement with the simulator’s selected test points within applicable tolerances. Philips identifies SpO2 monitoring as an important measurement for assessing oxygenation and emphasizes the importance of compatible, validated sensor performance. Expected outcome: The SpO2 channel operates consistently and passes the organization’s functional test requirements. If it passes, document the test values and return the device to service according to departmental policy.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Philips IntelliVue MX monitor displayed no SpO2 value and did not recognize the connected finger sensor.
CCR.Cause: Testing found an intermittent open connection in the SpO2 adapter cable; the monitor produced stable readings with a known-good compatible cable and simulator.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the defective SpO2 adapter cable, verified waveform, saturation, pulse rate, disconnect alarm, and recovery using an approved simulator, and returned the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: SpO2 technology installed: Philips FAST, Masimo, or Nellcor
Displayed technical alarm or INOP message
Whether the SpO2 parameter was visible and enabled
Simulator test values and displayed results

title: Philips IntelliVue MX Series Patient Monitor - NIBP Cuff Will Not Inflate or Measurement Fails
description: Troubleshooting failed NIBP measurements caused by cuff, hose, connector, patient conditions, settings, air leaks, obstructions, or acquisition hardware problems.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the IntelliVue monitor is the only device supporting an actively monitored patient. If blood pressure monitoring is clinically required: Notify the clinical team that NIBP measurements are unavailable or unreliable. Assess blood pressure using another approved device or method. Move the patient to another verified monitor when continued automatic NIBP monitoring is required. Do not repeatedly cycle the cuff on the patient during troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on the affected NIBP channel. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the monitor can be safely removed from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Attempt one NIBP measurement and observe the monitor, cuff, and displayed message. Determine whether: The cuff does not inflate at all. The cuff begins inflating but stops. The cuff inflates and then rapidly deflates. The measurement times out without displaying a result. The monitor displays an NBP equipment malfunction, loose cuff, weak signal, excessive motion, or similar message. The pump can be heard operating. The failure occurs in manual, automatic, or both measurement modes. Expected outcome: The failure pattern and any displayed message are documented. If the measurement completes normally, confirm operation with additional testing and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Cuff
steps.instructions: Remove the cuff from the patient and inspect it for: Tears, punctures, worn material, or separated seams. Damaged hook-and-loop fasteners. A twisted or folded bladder. Contamination or fluid intrusion. Incorrect cuff size. Loose or damaged cuff fittings. Use the correct cuff size for the intended patient population. An incorrectly sized or poorly applied cuff can prevent reliable oscillometric measurements. Expected outcome: The cuff is intact, correctly sized, and suitable for testing. If the cuff is damaged, replace it and repeat the measurement. If the issue is resolved, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect and Reconnect the NIBP Hose
steps.instructions: Check the entire hose from the cuff to the monitor or measurement module. Verify that: The hose is fully connected at both ends. The fittings are straight and secure. The hose is not kinked, pinched, cracked, stretched, or collapsed. The hose has not been trapped under equipment or furniture. No foreign material is visible inside the fittings. The hose is connected to the designated NBP connector. Philips MX-series configurations use compatible NBP cuffs and tubing connected to the appropriate NBP input; connector location can vary by monitor and measurement-module configuration. Expected outcome: An unobstructed, securely connected pneumatic pathway is established. If reconnecting or repositioning the hose resolves the failure, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Check for an External Air Leak
steps.instructions: Connect the cuff and hose, then start a measurement while the cuff is wrapped securely around an appropriate test mandrel or NIBP analyzer. Listen and feel for air escaping near: The cuff. Hose fittings. Quick-connect fittings. Hose bends. The monitor or module connection. A cuff that inflates briefly and rapidly loses pressure commonly indicates a pneumatic leak. Expected outcome: The cuff inflates and holds pressure during the measurement cycle without an obvious external leak. Replace any leaking cuff or hose and repeat the test. If the issue is resolved, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Substitute Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Replace the suspected accessories one at a time with compatible, known-good items: Known-good cuff. Known-good NIBP hose. Any approved adapter used in the connection. Do not substitute incompatible single-tube, dual-tube, neonatal, adult, or third-party components unless their compatibility has been verified for the installed NIBP configuration. Philips provides NBP cuffs and accessories designed and tested for use with its monitoring equipment. Expected outcome: The defective accessory is isolated without unnecessarily removing the monitor from service. If a known-good accessory restores normal measurements, replace the failed accessory, verify operation, and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 7. Verify Patient Category and NIBP Settings
steps.instructions: Open the NBP setup menu and verify: The selected patient category is correct: adult, pediatric, or neonatal. NBP measurement is enabled. The monitor is not in a mode that prevents the requested measurement. Automatic measurement intervals are configured appropriately. No active measurement is already running. The Start/Stop NBP control responds. Philips IntelliVue monitors allow NBP measurements to be initiated and automatic repeat intervals to be selected through the NBP setup controls. Expected outcome: The NIBP configuration matches the intended patient category and measurement mode. If correcting the settings resolves the issue, stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 8. Rule Out Motion and Patient-Related Conditions
steps.instructions: When clinically safe, have staff verify that: The patient is still during the measurement. The cuff is applied directly to the limb and not over thick clothing. The cuff is positioned correctly. The limb is supported. The patient is not experiencing shivering or significant movement. Perfusion is adequate at the selected limb. The cuff or hose is not being compressed. Oscillometric NIBP measurement depends on detecting pressure oscillations during controlled cuff inflation and deflation. Motion, weak pulsations, or improper cuff application may prevent completion. Expected outcome: Patient-related and application-related causes are ruled out. Do not repeatedly test on a patient solely to diagnose the device. Use an approved NIBP analyzer for continued evaluation.

steps.title: 9. Restart the Measurement Function
steps.instructions: Stop the current NIBP cycle and allow the cuff to deflate fully. Then: Disconnect and reconnect the hose. Confirm that no cuff pressure remains. Start one manual NIBP measurement. Observe the pump sound, inflation, deflation, and displayed messages. Expected outcome: A new measurement begins normally and completes without remaining stuck in the previous cycle. If normal operation returns, perform additional verification before returning the device to service.

steps.title: 10. Power-Cycle the Monitoring System
steps.instructions: Remove the monitor from patient use before restarting it. Follow the facility-approved shutdown and restart process for the monitor and any connected measurement module. After restart: Confirm that the NBP parameter appears. Check for equipment-malfunction or communication messages. Reconnect known-good NIBP accessories. Repeat functional testing. Expected outcome: A temporary software or communication condition is cleared. If the failure returns, continue troubleshooting rather than repeatedly restarting the monitor.

steps.title: 11. Test With an Approved NIBP Analyzer
steps.instructions: Connect the monitor to a calibrated NIBP analyzer using the correct test setup. Perform functional testing appropriate to facility policy, including: Inflation initiation. Controlled inflation and deflation. Leak or pressure-hold performance. Measurement completion. Displayed systolic, diastolic, and mean values. Overpressure protection testing when permitted by the approved procedure. Do not rely on a successful cuff inflation alone as proof that the NIBP system is accurate. Expected outcome: The NIBP system completes measurements and meets the facility’s accepted performance tolerances. If the device passes analyzer testing, investigate cuff application, accessories, patient conditions, and reported workflow before returning it to service.

steps.title: 12. Isolate the Monitor or Measurement Module
steps.instructions: If the MX-series configuration uses a detachable Multi-Measurement Module, X2, X3, or other supported acquisition device, determine where the NIBP hardware resides. When compatible equipment is available and facility procedures permit: Test the suspected measurement module on another compatible monitor. Test the monitor with a known-good compatible measurement module. Keep cuff and hose variables controlled during the comparison. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to the cuff, hose, acquisition module, monitor interface, or monitor system. Do not interchange modules without verifying compatibility and configuration requirements.

steps.title: 13. Inspect the NIBP Connector
steps.instructions: With the equipment powered down and removed from service, visually inspect the NIBP connector for: Physical damage. A loose connector body. Cracks. Bent or obstructed pneumatic fittings. Contamination or dried fluid. Evidence of impact. A connection that will not latch securely. Do not insert tools into the pneumatic port or attempt internal connector repair during initial troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The connector is clean, secure, and physically intact. If connector damage or contamination is found, remove the device or module from service and escalate it for repair.

steps.title: 14. Perform Final Operational Verification
steps.instructions: After correcting the identified cause: Repeat multiple NIBP measurements with an approved analyzer. Confirm normal inflation and controlled deflation. Confirm there are no persistent equipment-malfunction messages. Verify values are within the facility’s acceptable limits. Confirm automatic and manual modes as required. Inspect the cuff and hose after testing. Complete required safety and performance checks before release. Expected outcome: The NIBP function operates consistently and the device is safe to return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Philips IntelliVue MX monitor started an NIBP cycle, but the cuff would not inflate and no blood pressure result was displayed.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found a cracked NIBP hose near the cuff connector that allowed air to escape during inflation.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the damaged hose with a compatible known-good hose, completed repeated NIBP analyzer tests within facility tolerances, and returned the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact NBP message or failure behavior documented
External air leak found or ruled out
Unusual sounds, heat, or smell documented

title: Philips IntelliVue MX Series Patient Monitor - CO2 Module Not Recognized or No Capnogram
description: Troubleshooting missing CO2 detection or capnograms caused by module connections, sampling accessories, blockages, configuration, contamination, or communication failure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended troubleshooting while the IntelliVue monitor is the only device monitoring ventilation on an active patient. If continuous capnography is clinically required: Notify the clinical team immediately. Verify ventilation using another approved clinical method. Transfer CO2 monitoring to another verified monitor or capnography device. Do not assume a missing capnogram is only an equipment problem. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation continues to be assessed without relying on the unavailable CO2 parameter. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after the affected equipment can be safely removed from active patient use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Observe the CO2 parameter area and document whether the monitor shows: CO2 equipment or module not detected; No sensor or sampling line detected; Sampling line blocked; Water trap full, missing, or incorrectly installed; No breath detected; Dashed CO2 values; Numerical values without a waveform; Intermittent recognition. Also determine whether the issue began after cleaning, transport, accessory replacement, software changes, or connection to a different monitor. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified as a recognition, accessory, sampling, waveform, or configuration problem.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the CO2 Module or Measurement Device Connection
steps.instructions: Verify that the CO2 module, measurement extension, or connected acquisition device is fully seated in the supported Philips interface. Check for: A partially inserted module; Loose communication or interface cables; Bent, recessed, contaminated, or damaged connector contacts; Cracked housings; Evidence of liquid intrusion; Damaged cable strain relief. Disconnect and reconnect the device while the monitor is not supporting an active patient. Expected outcome: The monitor recognizes the CO2 hardware and displays the parameter. If recognized normally, perform a functional check and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Module Power and Status Indicators
steps.instructions: Observe the CO2 device for status lights, startup activity, audible pump operation, or displayed error messages. If no indicators or startup activity are present: Recheck the connection. Try another known-good compatible connection point, cable, or monitor when available. Confirm the monitor itself is operating normally. Expected outcome: The module powers up and completes initialization. A device that remains unpowered on multiple verified connections may require repair.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Sampling Line and Airway Accessories
steps.instructions: For sidestream CO2, inspect the complete sampling pathway, including: Sampling line; Airway adapter; Nasal cannula or patient interface; Water trap, if used; Connections at the module and patient end. Look for: Kinks; Blockages; Condensation; Secretions; Cracks; Loose fittings; Incorrect or incompatible accessories; An opened, contaminated, or previously used disposable line. Replace questionable disposable components with known-good Philips-compatible accessories. Expected outcome: The sampling pathway is open, properly connected, and free of contamination. If the capnogram returns, stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify the Water Trap or Inlet Assembly
steps.instructions: If the connected CO2 system uses a water trap: Confirm it is the correct type. Ensure it is fully installed. Check whether it is full, cracked, contaminated, or expired. Inspect the inlet area for moisture or debris without inserting tools into the port. Replace the water trap when its condition is uncertain. Expected outcome: The water trap is properly installed and the module no longer reports a trap or sampling error.

steps.title: 7. Listen for Normal Sampling Pump Operation
steps.instructions: For sidestream monitoring, listen for the expected sampling pump sound during operation. A silent pump, repeated startup cycling, abnormal grinding sound, or persistent occlusion alarm with an open known-good line may indicate an internal module problem. Do not open the module or attempt internal pump repair unless authorized and trained under the appropriate service procedure. Expected outcome: The pump operates consistently without abnormal noise or repeated occlusion messages.

steps.title: 8. Test With a Known-Good Sampling Accessory Set
steps.instructions: Install a known-good compatible sampling line, airway adapter, cannula, and water trap as applicable. Avoid changing multiple monitor settings during this test so the result clearly identifies whether the original accessories were responsible. Expected outcome: A waveform and numerical CO2 value appear. If so, remove the failed accessory from use and stop.

steps.title: 9. Verify the CO2 Parameter Is Enabled
steps.instructions: Confirm that the CO2 measurement is enabled and assigned to the correct parameter location or equipment source. Review for: A disabled CO2 measurement; A hidden waveform; An incorrect screen configuration; A parameter conflict; A patient category or profile change that removed CO2 from the display; An alternate CO2 source selected unintentionally. Do not alter institution-controlled profiles without authorization. Expected outcome: The CO2 parameter and waveform are visible and assigned to the connected measurement source.

steps.title: 10. Allow the Module to Complete Initialization
steps.instructions: Some CO2 devices require a startup or warm-up period before displaying valid data. After reconnecting the module: Allow initialization to complete. Observe for changing status messages. Do not repeatedly disconnect the device during startup. Verify that the monitor does not remain indefinitely in an initializing state. Expected outcome: The module completes startup and begins displaying a stable waveform and numerical value.

steps.title: 11. Check for Breath or Test-Gas Response Safely
steps.instructions: When permitted by hospital policy, test the CO2 channel using an approved simulator, test gas, or manufacturer-supported functional test method. Do not use exhaled breath testing when infection-control requirements prohibit it. Verify: The waveform appears promptly. The numerical value responds. The waveform returns to baseline appropriately. Occlusion or sampling alarms do not occur. Expected outcome: The CO2 system detects the approved test source and produces a stable capnogram.

steps.title: 12. Swap External Components One at a Time
steps.instructions: When compatible equipment is available, isolate the problem by testing one known-good item at a time: Sampling line; Water trap; Airway adapter; Module cable; CO2 module; Monitor or measurement interface. Do not place a suspect accessory onto an active patient. Expected outcome: The failure follows one external component, allowing it to be removed from service. If the issue remains with the original monitor or module, continue.

steps.title: 13. Perform a Controlled Power Restart
steps.instructions: After confirming the device is not being used for patient monitoring: Shut down the monitor normally. Disconnect and reseat the CO2 equipment. Restore power. Allow the monitor and module to complete startup. Check whether the CO2 parameter is recognized. Avoid repeated rapid power cycling. Expected outcome: Communication is restored and the CO2 parameter initializes normally. If the issue resolves, complete functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 14. Compare Operation on Known-Good Compatible Equipment
steps.instructions: Connect the suspect CO2 module to another compatible verified Philips monitor or interface when available. Also test a known-good compatible CO2 module on the original monitor. This helps distinguish between: A defective CO2 module; A damaged cable or interface; A monitor-side communication problem; A configuration issue. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to the module, connection path, or monitor.

steps.title: 15. Complete a Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: If the issue is corrected: Confirm the CO2 module remains recognized. Verify a stable waveform. Verify numerical response using an approved test method. Confirm sampling and occlusion alarms operate appropriately. Inspect for leaks or intermittent connections. Restore the approved clinical profile. Confirm there are no remaining technical alarms. Expected outcome: The CO2 function performs consistently and the monitor is safe to return to service.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Philips IntelliVue MX monitor did not recognize the connected CO2 module and displayed no capnogram.
CCR.Cause: Troubleshooting found a blocked and moisture-contaminated sidestream sampling line that prevented normal gas sampling.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the sampling line and water trap, confirmed a stable CO2 waveform using an approved functional test, and returned the monitor to service.

helpfulDetails: Approved simulator or test gas used

title: Philips IntelliVue MX Series Patient Monitor - Network Connection Loss or Duplicate IP Address
description: Troubleshooting central monitoring disconnects, network communication loss, and duplicate IP conflicts caused by cabling, wall ports, configuration, or network infrastructure.

steps.title: 1. Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not perform extended network troubleshooting while the IntelliVue monitor is the only device supporting an actively monitored patient. If central monitoring is required: Notify the clinical team that central monitoring or remote alarm notification may be unavailable. Confirm that alarms remain active and audible at the bedside. Maintain direct observation or transfer the patient to another verified monitoring device. Do not assume the central station is receiving alarms or patient data during a network failure. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring continues safely without relying on an unavailable network connection. Continue Clinical Engineering troubleshooting only after appropriate alternate monitoring has been established.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves: A network-disconnected or central-monitoring message; Loss of the patient sector at the Philips Information Center; Intermittent connection and reconnection; A duplicate IP address warning; Data available locally but missing at the central station; One affected monitor or multiple monitors in the same area; Wired Ethernet, wireless connectivity, or both. Record the exact message, affected bed, room, monitor serial number, and time of occurrence. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly identified as an isolated monitor issue, room-port issue, configuration conflict, or broader network event.

steps.title: 3. Verify Bedside Monitoring Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm that the monitor: Powers on normally; Displays local waveforms and numeric values; Produces bedside alarms; Responds normally to touchscreen or control inputs; Has not restarted, frozen, or entered a service condition. A network failure should not automatically be treated as a complete monitor failure. Expected outcome: Local patient monitoring functions remain operational. If local monitoring is also unreliable, remove the monitor from service and perform a separate functional evaluation.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Network Cable
steps.instructions: For a wired connection: Confirm the Ethernet cable is connected securely at the monitor and wall jack. Inspect both connector latches for damage. Check the cable for cuts, crushed sections, sharp bends, contamination, or stretched conductors. Disconnect and reconnect both ends until they lock securely. Confirm that the cable is connected to the approved clinical monitoring network port. Expected outcome: The network cable is intact and securely connected. If reconnecting the cable restores communication, verify central monitoring and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Check Network Link Indicators
steps.instructions: Observe the network port indicators, when visible. No link light may indicate a disconnected cable, defective cable, inactive wall port, or monitor network-interface problem. A link light without communication may indicate configuration, addressing, switch, VLAN, or central-system issues. Compare the indicator behavior with a functioning monitor in the same area. Expected outcome: A stable physical network link is present. Document whether the link indicator is off, steady, or flashing.

steps.title: 6. Test With a Known-Good Network Cable
steps.instructions: Replace the existing cable with an approved, known-good Ethernet cable. Do not use an unverified cable taken from another malfunctioning device. Expected outcome: The monitor reconnects using the known-good cable. If communication returns, replace the defective cable, verify operation, and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 7. Test the Wall Network Port
steps.instructions: Connect the monitor to a known-good clinical monitoring network port, following hospital network and infection-control procedures. Alternatively, test the original wall port using an approved network-testing method or another properly configured monitor. Do not connect the monitor to a general-purpose, guest, office, or unknown network jack. Expected outcome: The monitor communicates through the known-good port. If the monitor works on another port, leave the original port out of use and escalate the wall-port or switch-port issue to the appropriate network team.

steps.title: 8. Check for a Room-Specific or Area-Wide Outage
steps.instructions: Determine whether other IntelliVue monitors connected to the same room, network switch, nursing unit, central station, or wireless coverage area are experiencing the same problem. Expected outcome: The scope of the failure is established. If several monitors are affected, stop repeatedly restarting individual monitors. Escalate the probable network, switch, central-system, or infrastructure outage.

steps.title: 9. Confirm the Assigned Bed and Network Identity
steps.instructions: Verify that the monitor is assigned to the correct bed, room, unit, central station, and monitoring domain or clinical network. Check for recent monitor swaps, room moves, loaner installations, software servicing, or configuration replacement. Do not alter protected network settings without authorization and the approved Philips or hospital configuration process. Expected outcome: The monitor identity matches its physical location and intended central-station assignment.

steps.title: 10. Investigate a Duplicate IP Address Warning
steps.instructions: When a duplicate IP warning is displayed: Record the complete message and the monitor’s displayed network information. Determine whether another monitor was recently installed, moved, restored from backup, or returned from repair. Check whether two monitors may have received the same static configuration. Compare the affected monitor’s address with the hospital’s approved network inventory. Ask the network team to identify the other device using the address. Do not randomly assign a new IP address. Unauthorized changes may create additional conflicts or prevent communication with the monitoring system. Expected outcome: The conflicting device or incorrect network assignment is identified. Once the approved address is corrected by authorized personnel, restart or reconnect the monitor only as required by local procedure, then verify central communication.

steps.title: 11. Evaluate Wireless Connectivity, If Equipped
steps.instructions: For monitors using approved wireless connectivity: Confirm that wireless operation is enabled in the authorized configuration. Check whether the monitor connects normally in another known-good coverage area. Determine whether the failure occurs only in one room, hallway, elevator, or transport route. Inspect external wireless components or antennas for visible damage, when accessible. Check whether other wireless monitors are affected. Do not open the monitor or alter wireless security settings during floor-level troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The issue is identified as monitor-specific or coverage/infrastructure-related.

steps.title: 12. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: After patient safety has been addressed and cable, port, and configuration checks are complete: Disconnect the monitor from active patient use. Shut it down using the normal procedure. Wait for shutdown to complete. Restart the monitor. Observe network and central-station registration. Do not repeatedly power-cycle a monitor that continues to lose communication. Expected outcome: The monitor reconnects and remains visible at the central station. If restarting resolves the issue, continue observing long enough to confirm that the connection remains stable.

steps.title: 13. Verify Central-Station Communication
steps.instructions: Confirm with the clinical team or central-monitoring staff that: The correct patient appears in the correct sector. Waveforms and numeric values update normally. Bedside alarms are received centrally. Demographic and bed information are correct. No duplicate patient or duplicate bed assignment remains. Communication remains stable during an observation period. Expected outcome: Bidirectional monitoring workflow and alarm communication are restored. If successful, return the monitor to service and document the final configuration and test results.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the IntelliVue MX monitor repeatedly disconnected from the central station and displayed a duplicate IP address warning.
CCR.Cause: Inspection found that the monitor had the same static network address as a recently installed replacement monitor.
